wondering if the `PLDMFWPackagePayloadChecksum` should be added here as well since validating the payload checksum during parsing could be expensive with large component images.

The dicision of whether to validate the checksum or not while parsing, could be left to the consumer (e.g. a meson option in obmc/pldm).
Some of the use case might want to use the newer version of the package, but dosen't need that validation.
Also, it's hard to find a case that have to do the validation more than one time.

> The dicision of whether to validate the checksum or not while parsing, 
could be left to the consumer (e.g. a meson option in obmc/pldm).
Some of the use case might want to use the newer version of the package, but dosen't need that validation.

Agree, it has not been there before and code has been working fine without it.

ok, looks like the C library is already checking it in `src/dsp/firmware_update.c `

```
|       if (hdr->package_header_format_revision >=
|           PLDM_PACKAGE_HEADER_FORMAT_REVISION_FR04H) {
|       |       rc = pldm_edac_crc32_validate(package_payload_checksum,
|       |       |       |       |             package_payload_offset,
|       |       |       |       |             package_payload_size);
```

so user code need not check it.

I was wondering if it might be nice to have the checksums be part of the struct for debug or display purposes. But i do not have a real use-case right now.

Thanks for looking into this :)
